verdict: Dynatrace: Choose Dynatrace when enterprise full-stack observability with a DPS commit is the job — not Datadog host modules by default, and not PagerDuty. Scores use the IT & Development editorial methodology from first-party research as of 2026-08-18 — not hands-on product testing.
weaknesses: Heavier onboarding than New Relic Free
bestFor: Enterprises that will sign a DPS commit and deploy OneAgent broadly
SRE teams that want full-stack APM plus Davis AI in one platform
Buyers who already rejected per-host Datadog module math
notIdealFor: SMB teams that need a published $15/host tile (Datadog)
tradeoffs: Per-agent vs per-host vs per-seat vs per-GB pricing models
Module stacking and consumption overages vs single-SKU floors
Free tiers vs enterprise SSO/audit gates
Landscape-adjacent tools vs primary job-cluster peers on best pages
recommendation: Choose Dynatrace when enterprise full-stack observability with a DPS commit is the job — not Datadog host modules by default, and not PagerDuty. Compare Datadog or New Relic for published self-serve observability; PagerDuty for paging.
editorialNotes: IT Priority-3 batch. Approved on it-development-editorial v1.0.0. membershipRole=primary. jobCluster=observability-monitoring. handsOnTesting=false. Affiliate economics excluded.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Enterprise platform and OneAgent coverage — productive after architecture work, not in an afternoon. Not a lab test.
Full-stack observability — ranked with Datadog and New Relic, not against PagerDuty or GitHub.
APM, infra, logs, traces, and Davis AI form a deep SRE loop from vendor packaging.
Broad cloud/runtime ecosystem and webhooks; not a SaaS seat graph.
Enterprise security/compliance posture is a buying reason versus SMB observability tiles.
DPS commit + unlimited seats is how large estates buy.
Opaque vs Datadog’s published host SKU; rate-card transparency helps but commit size still dominates. Affiliate economics excluded.
Davis AI is a real observability assistant — scored as assistance, not as a reason to skip telemetry.

overallScoreRationale: Weighted average of the eight IT editorial criteria using category weights (IT job fit 16, workflow depth 14, ease of use 12, integrations 12, admin/security 12, value 12, AI 12, scalability 10), rounded to 1 decimal. Products are scored inside their job cluster — ITSM, observability, source control, hosting panels, and web-data platforms are not forced into one undifferentiated ranking. Not a hands-on lab score, and affiliate economics are excluded.
